drafted_by: Claude (session agent), on operator direction to run the backbone-train-mode arm before seed variance
standing_rule: Prose without a failing test always loses to a convenient default.
question: Holding everything fixed at the completed lr_1e-4 arm (EquiformerPoolFrontend cold_init, lr_frontend 1e-4, 400 steps, 12-fold LOSO, seed 0), does making the backbone's own Dropout (7 x p=0.1) and GraphDropPath (7 x 0.05) actually active during training change the locked M2 outcome or the train/held-out gap?

why_this_card.baseline_result: lr_1e-4 arm as run (git 3ce001a): FAIL_NO_SIGNAL. S1 pass (held-out mean macro-F1 0.4270), S2 8/12 vs 10 required. Train macro-F1 0.974 (0.960-0.987), mean train-min 0.935; mean train minus held-out gap 0.547. Single seed; 6/12 folds within 0.03 of the 0.40 bar.
why_this_card.finding: EquiformerPoolFrontend.train() calls self._backbone.eval() unconditionally (science/tokyo_eye/v8/equiformer_pool_frontend.py:153-156). Verified: 0/14 regularization modules in train mode after system.train() (scripts/diag_gradflow_pool_frontend.py --mode verify-train-mode). The baseline arm therefore trained an unfrozen ~30M-parameter backbone with its own regularization off.
why_this_card.hypothesis_status: CANDIDATE contributor to the train/held-out gap, UNTESTED. The rates are mild (0.1 / 0.05) relative to an 11-structure (~3.3k residue) training set on ~30M parameters, so the size of any effect is unknown. Other contributors -- very small training set, the intentional edge_type->label leak, cold init -- are not ruled out. This card measures the effect of this one change; it does not presuppose the effect is large.
why_this_card.fix: Instance-level override in the runner (apply_backbone_train_mode): system.frontend.train is bound to nn.Module.train, so system.train() reaches the backbone. equiformer_pool_frontend.py is NOT modified, so the file pins of the completed arms stay valid.

isolation_discipline.single_variable: backbone_train_mode: False in the baseline (lr_1e-4) arm, True here.
identical_to_baseline: evaluation under system.eval() (all regularization off, as in the baseline)
isolation_discipline.baseline_comparability_caveat: The baseline is one seed-0 run. GPU nondeterminism means a same-config rerun is not guaranteed bit-identical, and no seed-to-seed variance estimate exists yet. Comparison to the baseline is therefore descriptive; see interpretation_rule.
isolation_discipline.amendment_rule: Any change to locked bars, steps, seed, frontend, max_neighbors, lr values, or the arm definition requires a new signed card, not an edit to this one.

interpretation_rule.status: PROPOSED -- operator to confirm or change BEFORE seal; the numbers are judgment calls, not derived

interpretation_rule.comparison_to_baseline: Descriptive until a seed-variance estimate exists (planned follow-up: seed 1 on the first six folds in canonical order, fixed before any result).

reading_bands.clear_effect: mean train minus held-out gap falls by >= 0.10 from 0.547 AND (S1 mean or S2 count improves on 0.4270 / 8)
reading_bands.not_distinguishable_from_noise: anything else. This is NOT evidence that regularization is irrelevant -- only that a single-seed comparison cannot separate a small effect from run-to-run noise.
reading_bands.worse: S1 mean and S2 count both worse than baseline: report as observed, single seed; do not explain away.
